Diagnosis: `_equal_sign` (`=[^\S\r\n]*`) consumes whitespace after `=`, so for `KEY= # explanation` the value part starts at `#`; `parse_unquoted_value`'s strip regex `\s+#.*` then finds no preceding whitespace and returns `"# explanation"` instead of `""`.

Change plan (parser.py only): revert `_equal_sign` to `=` so the leading space remains in the value part, and keep `parse_unquoted_value` stripping a comment only when whitespace precedes `#` via `re.sub(r"\s+#.*", "", part).rstrip()`. This yields `KEY= # explanation` → `""`, while `KEY=#literal` → `"#literal"` and `KEY=a#b` → `"a#b"` stay literal. Quoting, exports, and ordinary comments are unaffected since `_comment`/`_end_of_line` still handle trailing comments.
